question: What is the correct order for checking a patient's tummy during a physical exam?
explanation: You listen (auscultation) before you tap or press! If you touch the tummy first, you might change the natural bowel sounds and get a false reading. You've got this! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why do nurses listen with a stethoscope before pressing or tapping on a patient's abdomen?

options.A: To follow hospital rules without any clinical reason
options.B: To make the patient feel more comfortable and relaxed
options.C: To prevent altering natural bowel sounds before listening
options.D: To ensure the procedure takes as little time as possible

explanation: Spot on! Pressing or tapping too early wakes up the tummy and makes sounds that weren't there originally. Always listen first! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h1)

question: What kind of stool do you usually see when someone has bleeding in their upper gut (like the stomach)?

options.A: Bright red streaks on the surface
options.C: Dark, tarry stools known as melena

explanation: When blood travels all the way from the upper digestive tract, digestive juices break it down and turn it dark and sticky like tar by the time it comes out. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h2)

question: A patient takes painkillers for joint pain every day and suddenly complains of a burning stomach. What's the most likely cause?

options.A: A normal reaction that requires no further action
options.B: An allergic reaction causing skin rashes
options.D: A complete blockage of the large intestine

explanation: Common pain meds (like NSAIDs) can wear down the protective lining of the stomach, leading to irritation and burning pain. Good to watch out for in clinical practice! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which part of your stethoscope is best for listening to bowel sounds?
explanation: The flat diaphragm is specially designed to pick up high-pitched sounds like bowel activity. You're building great clinical skills! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h3)

question: You listen to all four areas of a patient's tummy for five full minutes and hear zero sounds. What does this mean?

options.A: Absent bowel sounds indicating decreased motility
options.C: Mild gas trapped in the lower colon
options.D: Hyperactive sounds due to recent eating

explanation: Total silence for a full five minutes is a red flag! It usually means the intestines have slowed right down or stopped moving. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why is sudden, unexplained weight loss a big warning sign in digestive health?

options.A: It means the patient is simply exercising too much
options.B: It shows that digestion is working much faster than normal
options.C: It often points to chronic malabsorption or underlying disease
options.D: It is a harmless change that happens as people age

explanation: When the gut struggles to absorb nutrients, or an illness burns through energy, the body weight drops quickly. It's an important clue for nurses! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h4)

question: During a digestive check, which physical sign is best for quickly spotting dehydration?

options.A: Moisture of the oral mucous membranes
options.B: The presence of minor scars on the skin
options.C: The temperature of the lower legs
options.D: The exact color of the client's hair

explanation: Checking inside the mouth! Dry or sticky gums and tongue are quick, reliable signs that a patient is losing too much fluid from vomiting or diarrhea. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h4)

question: Which simple test helps find hidden blood in a patient's stool?
explanation: The word 'occult' means hidden! This stool test catches tiny traces of blood that your eyes can't see. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why does a doctor order liver function blood tests for a patient with upper tummy pain?

options.A: To measure the exact amount of food remaining in the stomach
options.B: To see if the patient has a normal blood pressure
options.C: To check for inflammation or damage in the liver and biliary system
options.D: To determine how quickly the kidneys are filtering waste

explanation: When liver cells or bile ducts get irritated or damaged, they leak specific enzymes into the blood. The lab tests catch this! Great job thinking clinically. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h5)

question: Your patient just came back from an upper endoscopy. What must you check FIRST before offering them a sip of water?

options.A: If the skin color is completely normal
options.B: Whether the bowel sounds are hyperactive
options.C: If the patient can walk to the bathroom
options.D: The return of the gag reflex

explanation: Safety first! The throat spray numbs the swallow reflex, so giving water too early could cause them to choke. Always test the gag reflex first. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h6)

question: Why is it so important to document your assessment findings right after finishing the exam?

options.A: To ensure accurate records and safe continuity of care
options.B: To finish paperwork so the shift can end quickly
options.C: To satisfy hospital administrators who review charts
options.D: To prevent the patient from asking questions later

explanation: Writing things down right away stops you from forgetting key details and keeps the whole healthcare team on the same page. You're thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h6)
